question: Will AfD win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: The ensemble baseline (2%) is modest; considering upside risks, we adjust slightly upward.
Polling data still show CDU/Greens ahead of AfD in the 18–29% band, making AfD leading in seats unlikely.
Upside risks include potential undercounting of AfD support, turnout surges, and late campaign swings, but none imply a high-probability threshold breach.
Historical base-rate for AfD leading BW is low, though not impossible given current spreads.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections document credible upside risks (undercounting, turnout, late swing) but do not indicate a high-confidence path to AfD leading; the baseline remains low.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted upward from 0.02 to 0.04 to incorporate modest upside risk from polling undercount and turnout dynamics; set range 0.02–0.07 to reflect uncertainty.

forecasts.reference-class: Baden-Württemberg Landtag (state) elections under Germany's mixed-member proportional representation; historically the AfD has not been the largest party in BW elections, with CDU or Greens typically leading.

causal-factors.name: CDU lead and AfD around 18-20% in latest Baden-Württemberg polls
causal-factors.rationale: February 2026 Infratest dimap polls show CDU ~28%, Greens ~27%, AfD ~18% (with others around 8.5%), indicating AfD is not the largest party on current survey data. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate: AfD has never won the most seats in BW
causal-factors.rationale: In 2021 AfD received 9.7% and 17 seats, while Greens and CDU led the field, implying a long-run base-rate against AfD being the largest party in BW. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Baden-W%C3%BCrttemberg_state_election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Current intra-state momentum favors CDU/Greens with AfD around 18–20%
causal-factors.rationale: Across late Jan–Feb 2026 polls, CDU remains the leading party with Greens close behind and AfD near 18–20%, keeping AfD from leading in seats. ([swp.de](https://www.swp.de/baden-wuerttemberg/landtagswahl-2026-gruene-holen-auf-afd-verliert-cdu-stabil-das-zeigt-eine-neue-umfrage-78594088.html?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Coalition dynamics and mainstream party exclusion of AfD reduces practical dominance
causal-factors.rationale: Historically, BW coalitions have excluded the AfD from government, reducing the likelihood that AfD could convert a top vote share into governing power, even if it approached top status. ([bundeswahlleiterin.de](https://www.bundeswahlleiterin.de/en/service/landtagswahlen/land-8.html?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead vs AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Late-2025 to early-2026 polls place CDU roughly 8–11 percentage points ahead of AfD (e.g., CDU ~28–29%, AfD ~18–20%), making AfD the largest party in BW unlikely unless a sharp reversal occurs.

causal-factors.name: Greens holding or closing gap with AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Greens polling around 23% (and sometimes near AfD) reduces AfD's relative advantage, lowering the odds of AfD being the largest party even if CDU remains ahead.

causal-factors.name: Historical base rate and past results in BW
causal-factors.rationale: AfD has not been the largest party in Baden-Württemberg in recent elections (2021: 9.7%, 17 seats), so the long-run baseline probability of AfD leading the state is low.

causal-factors.name: Turnout volatility and mobilization effects
causal-factors.rationale: A higher turnout could disproportionately mobilize voters in some blocs and temporarily lift AfD beyond current averages.

causal-factors.name: Polling methodology and potential undercounting of AfD supporters
causal-factors.rationale: If AfD supporters are underrepresented in surveys, actual support could be higher than measured, providing upside risk to the probability of AfD leading.

causal-factors.name: Unexpected local issues or campaign shocks affecting CDU/Greens
causal-factors.rationale: A sudden controversy or policy setback affecting CDU or Greens could tilt vote shares temporarily in AfD's favor, pushing the probability of leading upward.

causal-factors.name: AfD overtakes CDU/Greens in polls (survey lead)
causal-factors.rationale: A sustained swing of roughly 4–6 percentage points toward AfD that flips it into the lead over CDU/Greens would increase its seat share under Baden-Württemberg's mixed-member proportional system.

causal-factors.name: High AfD turnout / mobilization
causal-factors.rationale: If AfD-supporters turn out at higher rates than CDU/Greens voters, AfD's vote share could rise enough to challenge or exceed the leading party in seats.

causal-factors.name: CDU/Greens decline due to issues
causal-factors.rationale: Negative developments affecting CDU or Greens support could widen the gap with AfD, reducing the likelihood of AfD being largest.

causal-factors.name: Polling undercount / methodological bias favoring AfD
causal-factors.rationale: If polls systematically undercount AfD support due to sampling biases, actual support could be higher and raise its probability of leading.

synthesis: Upside risks identified by objections are plausible but not strong enough to place AfD as the clear largest party. The calibrated probability remains modest (around 4%), reflecting evidence that AfD leading in the BW Landtag is unlikely but not impossible.
